content.text:
I've inspected every responsive location. No commitment mechanic exists anywhere; the Agreement affirmatively disclaims one.

**Findings from the sweep:**
- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** — express no-minimum, pay-for-what-you-order language, plus a statement that declining a further Order Form is "not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 12.3 (p0051)** — Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** — bars Vendor from imposing minimum-use charges not stated in the Order Form.
- **§ 8.2–8.3, § 9.4** — renewal is opt-out with an exit and no ratchet; without-cause termination leaves only accrued Fees payable with prepaid Fees refunded, so no residual take-or-pay.
- **§ 7.7 (p0032)** — late-payment liquidated damages; that is a payment-terms issue, not a minimum commitment, so I am not flagging it here.

Nothing binds us to purchase volume, and the clauses located benefit us — no redline is warranted.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement sits at our preferred position, so no redline is needed. Section 2.1 expressly states that "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies" and that "Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form," and it confirms that a decision not to place a further Order Form is "not a breach or shortfall" — there is no take-or-pay, minimum spend, or shortfall mechanic to narrow. Section 12.3 reinforces this by having Vendor acknowledge that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," and Section 7.1 bars Vendor from imposing any "minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify." Nor is a commitment reintroduced indirectly: quantities are set only in an Order Form (§ 1.9), renewal is opt-out on thirty days' notice with a capped uplift (§§ 8.2–8.3), and § 9.4 lets us terminate without cause owing only accrued Fees with prepaid Fees refunded. Because the preferred elements are met on the document's face, the fallback true-up/reduction mechanics are unnecessary. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-terms issue rather than a volume commitment, and the § 9.4 exit economics belong to the termination-for-convenience rule, so neither is treated as a MINCOMMIT deviation here.
